title: Model binding: hybrid selector resolution order & graceful fallbacks for tag/semver/sha
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define deterministic resolution semantics for model selectors supplied via API/SDK. Support hybrid selectors: explicit tag (e.g., 'stable'), semver ranges (e.g., '^1.4.0'), and commit sha (40-char). Ensure client-side and server resolvers converge and provide transparent fallback and telemetry. This ticket codifies precedence, error surface, TTLs/caching, and migration guidance to minimize surprises when models are updated or archived.
acceptance_criteria: Server resolver implements precedence: exact sha > exact semver exact match > semver range (highest satisfying) > tag alias > experimental fallback policy
SDK resolves locally cached pinned refs within TTL and fallbacks to server when expired; provides clear error codes for ambiguous selectors
Model resolution logs emitted with selector, resolved-ref, resolution-path, latency and cache-hit flag
Compatibility test harness validating 12 scenarios (sha/tag/semver conflicts, deleted refs, version ranges)
Migration doc for customers describing how to migrate from tag-only pins to semver-aware pins
technical_decision_log: 2025-03-10: Agreed on deterministic precedence after RFC review — prefer strongest identity first (sha) to guarantee immutability.
2025-03-11: Chose semver highest-satisfying strategy over 'latest' tag for range selectors to avoid non-deterministic upgrades.
2025-03-12: Opted for 5-minute client-local TTL with server Cache-Control header to balance freshness and lookup cost (tunable per account).
Tradeoff: longer TTL reduces lookups but delays urgent rollbacks; mitigated by server-initiated invalidation for high-priority incidents.
